en: The Sutra of the Vimalaprabhāsa-mahādhāraṇī, translated by the Tripitaka Master Mitrasena of India during the Tang Dynasty by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard. At one time the Buddha was staying in the Great Monastery in the city of Kapilavastu, together with...
There was a great assembly of bhikṣus numbering in the hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of nayutas.
There were also immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
among whom were such as the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin.
The Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
and the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,
Akṣayamati Bodhisattva,
and Maitreya Bodhisattva.
These were the leaders among them.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable numbers of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others.
He was surrounded by a vast assembly of beings who paid him respectful homage as he preached the Dharma.
At that time, there was a great brahmin in that city named Kāśyapa Jñātṛ.
Having returned to and venerated the non-Buddhist paths while disbelieving the Buddha-dharma,
there was a skilled physiognomist who addressed him, saying:
"Great Brahmin, seven days from now you will surely meet your end."
When the brahmin heard these words, his heart was filled with grief and distress;
struck by alarm and fear, he reflected: "Who can save me? Upon whom shall I rely?"
He further thought: "The śramaṇa Gautama claims to be omniscient and has realized omniscience.
I shall go to him;
if he is indeed truly omniscient,"
"He will surely speak of my distress and fears.
Having formed this thought, he went at once to the place where the Buddha was and gazed from afar upon the Tathāgata before the assembled multitude.
He desired to inquire but harbored hesitation.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, who clearly perceives all phenomena of the three periods of time without exception,
knew the thoughts in the brahmin’s mind.
With a voice of loving-kindness and gentleness, he addressed him, saying:
"Great Brahmin, seven days from now you shall certainly meet your end.
You will fall into the terrifying Avīci Hell, and from there you will further enter the sixteen hells."
Having emerged from that state, they again receive the body of a caṇḍāla;
after the end of their life there, they are reborn among pigs,
where they constantly dwell in foul mud and perpetually feed upon excrement and filth.
Throughout their long lifespans, they undergo manifold sufferings;
later, when they obtain human form, they are poor and lowly,
foul-smelling and impure, with an ugly appearance, dark and emaciated.
Wasted and afflicted with leprosy, they take no pleasure in being seen;
their throats are like needles, perpetually lacking food and drink;
and when struck by others, they undergo great suffering and distress.
When the brahmin heard these words,
he was seized with great terror; weeping and filled with sorrow,
he hastened to the Buddha’s presence and prostrated at his feet.
He addressed the Buddha, saying, "The Tathāgata is indeed the savior of all sentient beings.
I now repent my transgressions and take refuge in the World-Honored One.
I only pray that you will rescue me from the suffering of the great hells."
The Buddha said, "Great Brahmin, at the junction of the three roads in this city of Kapilavastu, there is an ancient stūpa of a past Buddha.
Within it, the relics of the Tathāgata are present.
That stūpa has fallen into ruin; you should go there and restore it."
Furthermore, having fashioned the spire and shaft of the *cakra*,
one should inscribe the *dhāraṇī* within it and perform great offerings.
According to the ritual, one should recite the divine mantra seven times.
May your life-force be restored and increased;
when your lifespan eventually ends, you shall be reborn in the realm of Sukhāvatī,
where you will experience supreme bliss for hundreds of thousands of kalpas.
Thereafter, he again experienced pleasure for hundreds of thousands of kalpas in the world-system of Abhirati, just as before;
subsequently, he resided in the various Tuṣita celestial palaces.
Furthermore, for hundreds of thousands of kalpas, they will continuously experience bliss;
in all places of birth, they will constantly remember their past lives;
all obstacles will be eliminated, and all transgressions will be extinguished.
They shall forever be free from all sufferings such as those of the hells;
they shall constantly behold the Buddhas and always be sustained and protected by the Tathāgatas.
O Brahmin, if there be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, or any sons and daughters of good family who...
If there are those who have short lifespans or suffer from many illnesses,
they should repair old stupas or construct small clay stupas,
and transcribe dharani mantras according to the ritual rules.
By constructing a ritual altar with a mantra-empowered cord,
those whose lives are nearing their end shall have their lifespan further extended through this merit.
All those suffering from various illnesses shall attain complete recovery;
they shall forever leave behind the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts,
such that even the sound of hell shall no longer be heard by their ears.
How much more so for the body itself?
Having heard these words, the brahmin was filled with joy and immediately desired to go to the site of that ruined stūpa to carry out the restoration according to the instructions.
At that time, within the assembly, the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin rose from his seat,
joined his palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
what is this dharma of the dhāraṇī?"
And it is able to cause the roots of merit and goodness to grow. The Buddha said:
"There is a great dhāraṇī called the Dharma of the Supreme, Stainless, Pure Radiance Great Maṇḍala."
The Buddhas use this to comfort sentient beings.
If there are those who hear this dhāraṇī,
they shall extinguish the sins of the five heinous crimes and close the gates of hell.
It eradicates the defilements of stinginess, greed, and envy;
those with short lifespans shall all attain longevity;
and no auspicious undertaking shall fail to be accomplished.
Then the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, we pray that the Buddha will expound this dharma of the dhāraṇī,
so that all sentient beings may attain long life."
In order to purify all karmic obstacles of sin and to act as a great illumination for all sentient beings,
at that time the World-Honored One, having heard this request, [consented].
Immediately, he emitted a great radiance from the crown of his head,
which illuminated the entire trichiliocosm and fully awakened all the Tathāgatas.
It returned to its original place and entered through the crown of the Buddha's head.
Then the Buddha, with a voice as beautiful, pleasing, and melodious as that of the kalaviṅka bird,
spoke this mantra:

"Āvaraṇaviskambhin, this is the root dhāraṇī mantra."
If one wishes to perform this rite,
it should be done on the eighth, thirteenth,
fourteenth, or fifteenth day of the month.
Circumambulate the śarīra stūpa seventy-seven times to the right.
Recite this dhāraṇī seventy-seven times as well.
One should then construct an altar and maintain ritual purity upon it.
Transcribe this dhāraṇī seventy-seven times.
Out of respect for the Dharma, one should offer incense,
flowers, food and drink, clean robes, and perform ritual ablutions for the scribe.
One should offer worship with scented ointments and incense,
or bestow the seven precious jewels, or give according to one's capacity.
One should hold the root mantra and place it within the stūpa to worship this stūpa.
Alternatively, one may fashion seventy-seven small clay stupas and place a single copy [of the scripture] within each stupa,
making offerings according to the ritual. Having performed this in accordance with the Dharma,
the lifespan of one whose life is about to end shall be further extended.
All karmic obstacles from previous lives and all actions leading to the evil realms will be completely extinguished.
One shall forever be free from the hells, the realm of hungry ghosts, and the animal realm,
and wherever one is born, one will always remember past lives.
All their aspirations shall be fully realized;
they will have already planted roots of goodness in the presence of seventy-seven billion Tathāgatas.
All illnesses and all afflictions shall be entirely eliminated.
If there is a person whose illness is grave and whose life is about to end, one should construct a square mandala for them.

Upon it, one should draw various shapes, namely: the form of a wheel, the form of a vajra, the form of a conch, the form of a trident, the form of a crescent moon, and the form of a lotus. At the four corners, one should draw lotuses upon which vases are placed; these vases are filled with scented water and set at the four corners.
Arrange incense burners and burn various kinds of famous incense.

Fill five-colored bowls with various foods and the "three white foods"—namely milk, curd, and non-glutinous rice—and further fill five bowls with fragrant flowers, water, and non-glutinous rice to offer upon the altar.
Place various kinds of food and drink, filling one vessel,
along with a single jar of water, at the center of the altar.
Near the edge of the altar, draw an image of a Vināyaka.
Place a lamp upon the crown [of the head].
Position the patient to the west of the maṇḍala,
facing toward it.
Place a vessel filled with food before the patient upon the altar.
The mantra-reciter must be pure and act according to the Dharma;
he shall recite the mantra over this patient seventy-seven times.
It causes a person who is about to die to remain in a state of unconsciousness for seven days,
after which their life is sustained and consciousness returns as if awakening from a dream.
If one recites this once every day while maintaining purity and ritual cleanliness, [the same result shall follow].
If one recites and maintains this mantra for a full hundred years,
that person will, at the end of life, be reborn in the realm of Sukhāvatī.
If one constantly recites and maintains it at all times, [the same result shall follow].
Until they reach enlightenment, they will constantly remember their past lives,
forever remaining free from premature death and all evil realms.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who recites the name of a deceased person, [they shall likewise attain these benefits].
If one recites this mantra with a sincere heart seventy-seven times,
should that deceased person have fallen into an evil realm,
they shall immediately be freed from the suffering of the miserable paths and be reborn in heaven to experience bliss.
Alternatively, one may write out this dhāraṇī according to the ritual manual while reciting the deceased's name,
place it within a Buddhist stūpa, and make offerings in accordance with the Dharma;
this will also cause the deceased to escape the evil realms and be reborn in the heavens.
Or they may be reborn in the Tuṣita heaven palace;
until they attain bodhi, they shall not fall into the evil realms.
If there are good men or good women, [who...]
Those who circumambulate this stupa to the right, or prostrate before it, or make offerings to it,
shall receive the prediction of their attainment of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and shall never regress.
All past obstructions and all sinful karmas shall be completely extinguished.
Even those who have fallen among the classes of birds or beasts,
upon reaching the shadow of this stupa, shall forever be liberated from the evil realms of animal existence.
If one has committed the five sins of immediate retribution,
they shall all be extinguished by being within the shadow of the stūpa or by touching that stūpa.
At the place where the stūpa is situated, there will be no malevolent spirits, yakṣas, or rākṣasas.
There shall be no pūtanas, piśācas, and the like;
nor any fierce beasts, evil dragons, venomous insects, or poisonous plants;
nor any mātaras, or various malevolent spirits and ghosts who steal vital essence.
Furthermore, there shall be no calamities of war, fire, water, frost, hail, or famine,
nor any occurrences of untimely death, evil dreams, or inauspicious suffering.
Should any such evil omens appear within that land, [they shall be averted].
That stūpa immediately manifested supernatural transformations and emitted great flames of light,
causing all those evil and inauspicious matters to be utterly extinguished.
Furthermore, as for those sentient beings who harbored malicious intentions toward it...
Or if enemies, their allies, or various types of robbers and bandits seek to destroy this kingdom,
that stūpa will likewise emit great flames of fire.
Immediately at that spot, various weapons will appear;
upon seeing them, the wicked thieves will naturally retreat and disperse.
Furthermore, all the devas and benevolent spirits will constantly protect that kingdom.
A great boundary was established extending one hundred yojanas in each direction around the country;
within it, there were no epidemics, afflictions, or strife among men, women, or even animals.
One shall not perform any unlawful acts.
Nothing else can destroy it through incantations or sorcery.
This is called the Root Dhāraṇī Method.
"Good son, I shall now explain for you the *dhāraṇī* method for the central shaft of the *cakra* (wheel). It is as follows:

Oṃ sarvatathāgatavipulaye ṭiṭṭi maṇikarṇaka-harañcita vipuṣṭaye ṭiṭṭi tura tura samantavilokite sara sara pāpa-viśodhani puṣṭani sapuṣṭani pravaraye ṭiṭṭi vare maṇitroṭe hulu-ciramare viśuddhe hūṃ hūṃ svāhā. Good son, you should practice this according to the Dharma."
Transcribe this mantra ninety-nine times and install them around the four sides of the central axis of the stupa.
Furthermore, transcribe this mantra along with the methods for its efficacy.
Having thus placed it securely, covered over at the center of the shaft,
one then establishes ninety-nine thousand *cakra* (wheel) shafts.
He has also enshrined ninety-nine thousand relics of the Buddhas;
he has also already constructed ninety-nine thousand stupas for the relics of the Buddhas;
and he has also already constructed ninety-nine thousand great stupas of the eight precious substances.
Furthermore, it is as if one has already constructed ninety-nine thousand stūpas for the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa).
If one constructs even a single small mud stūpa and places this dhāraṇī within it, [the merit is likewise attained].
This constitutes having already constructed ninety-nine thousand minor jeweled stupas.
If there are sentient beings who circumambulate these stupas to the right,
or prostrate once, or join their palms once;
Whether one offers a single flower or a single incense,
or makes offerings with burning incense, unguents, bells, banners, and canopies,
it is as if one has already made offerings to ninety-nine thousand stupas of the Buddhas.
This constitutes the accomplishment of a vast accumulation of roots of goodness and merit.
If even flying birds, mosquitoes, gadflies, or flies should enter the shadow of the stupa,
they shall receive the prediction of their attainment of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and shall never regress.
If one sees this stūpa from afar, or hears the sound of its bells, or even hears its name,
all the five crimes of immediate retribution and every obstacle of sin committed by that person shall be completely extinguished.
They shall always be protected and remembered by all Buddhas and attain the pure path of the Tathāgatas;
this is called the Dharma of the Cakrākṣara Dhāraṇī.
"Good son, I shall now explain for you the dharani method for constructing a Buddha stupa. It is as follows:

Oṃ sarvatathāgatamālāviśuddhe gandhavilepani pratīccha saṃskāra tathāgatadhātu dhāri dhāri dharadharā saṃdhāra saṃdhāra sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhite svāhā. If there be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās..."
Whether one builds a stūpa oneself or instructs others to build one;
whether one repairs an old stūpa or constructs a small one;
whether made of clay or using bricks and stone.
One should first recite the mantra one thousand and eight times before constructing it.
As for the dimensions of the stupa, they may be as small as a fingernail,
or as large as one cubit, up to a yojana.
By the power of that mantra and through the sincerity of his heart,
a wondrous fragrance issued forth from the mud and other materials within the stupa—
namely, ox-head sandalwood, red sandalwood, and white sandalwood.
By personally using or instructing others to use dragon’s brain, musk, saffron,
and other celestial fragrances, one shall achieve a vast accumulation of roots of goodness and merit.
If one's life is short, it shall be extended;
at the time of death, one will behold ninety-nine billion hundred thousand nayutas of Buddhas,
and one will always be remembered by all those Buddhas.
He was then granted the prediction of rebirth in the realm of Sukhāvatī,
where his lifespan would be ninety-nine billion hundred-thousand nayutas of years;
there he would constantly possess the recollection of past lives, the divine eye, the divine body, the divine ear, and the divine nose.
Heavenly sandalwood fragrance emanates from his body,
and his mouth constantly emits the scent of the utpala flower.
Having attained the five supernormal powers, he is non-retrogressive in his progress toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
If one applies consecrated fragrant clay— even if it is extremely small,
only as much as a mustard seed— upon this stūpa,
that person shall likewise obtain the great mass of merit described above.
If bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās transcribe this dhāraṇī method according to the Dharma,
they should honor and make offerings to it with a pure mind, no differently than they would to the Buddha himself.
One should also provide superior offerings to the person who has transcribed it.
Having transcribed the mantras and seals as previously described,
one should place them within a stūpa, inside a stūpa being constructed, or within the central shaft of a *cakra* (parasol), thereby accomplishing them according to the Dharma.
This person shall obtain a vast accumulation of roots of goodness and merit.
When the Buddha spoke this dharani-seal method,
all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions praised him with one voice, saying:
Excellent, excellent, Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha!
You have been able to skillfully expound this Great Dhāraṇī Seal Dharma,
so that no sentient being shall pass away in vain.
They shall obtain great benefit and gather a vast mass of merit,
even reaching the point of non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, among the assembly were the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of supernatural beings.
As well as the various bodhisattvas and Vajradharas;
the Four Kings, Śakra, and Brahmā;
Nārāyaṇa and Maheśvara.
Maṇibhadra, Pūrṇabhadra, as well as the deities Virūḍhaka, Yama, Virūpākṣa,
Vaiśravaṇa, Vāsava, and the assembly of various ṛṣis.
Having heard this Dharma, they gave rise to a mind of weary detachment;
becoming subdued and gentle,
they were filled with great joy and addressed one another with loud voices.
How rare, how rare are all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas!
How rare, how rare is the truly sublime and wondrous Dharma!
How rare, how rare is this dharani-seal method!
What the Tathāgata has spoken is extremely difficult to encounter.
At that time, the great Brahmin Kapphiṇa heard this Dharma-seal of the Great Dhāraṇī,
which possesses such great merit and supreme benefits.
He immediately attained clear penetration of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), becoming free from dust and defilement;
severing all afflictions and extinguishing all karmic obstacles, his lifespan was extended,
and he gave rise to immeasurable joy and exultation.
"May all sentient beings likewise attain purity of mind and intention.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin took up a precious dais,
adorned with various jewels interspersed and arrayed in manifold ways.
Adorning themselves with the adornments of a Buddha,
they venerated the Tathāgata out of their love for the Dharma;
they circumambulated him three times to the right and prostrated at his feet.
He addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, this Dharma-seal of the Great Dhāraṇī Maṇḍala is extremely difficult to encounter.
World-Honored One, you have taught this treasury of the sublime Dharma for all sentient beings to serve as a seal of protection for Jambudvīpa."
To cause all sentient beings to plant great roots of goodness,
to bestow upon them longevity, and to extinguish their afflictions;
I, too, shall now act for the sake of causing sentient beings to plant roots of goodness.
In order to make offerings to all the Tathāgatas,
I now, before the Buddha, shall proclaim the dharma of the *dhāraṇī* of the Seal of One’s Own Mind.
He then spoke the mantra as follows:
Namo bhagavate nāvanatīnām samyaksambuddha-koṭi-nayuta-śatasahasrāṇām | Namo sarva-nīvaraṇa-viṣkambhi-bodhisattvāya | Oṃ tura tura |

Sarvavināraṇa-viśvañji-ni svāhā. Sarvapāpa-viśodhani svāhā.
World-Honored One, this dhāraṇī was spoken by ninety-nine billion Buddhas.
If there are those who, with a sincere heart, recite this even for a brief moment,
all their sinful karmas will be completely extinguished.
If there are those who transcribe this mantra according to the Dharma, [the same shall occur].
Having filled ninety-nine volumes [of the scripture], place them within the stūpa or around its perimeter.
Should someone prostrate to it, offer praise, or make offerings of incense, flowers, unguents, lamps, and candles to this stūpa; [they shall obtain great merit].
Those sons or daughters of good family, within their present life,
shall extinguish all sins, remove all obstacles, and fulfill all aspirations;
they will thereby have already made offerings to ninety-nine billion hundred-thousand nayutas of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River.
Furthermore, having made offerings to stupas containing the relics of ninety-nine billion hundred-thousand nayutas of Ganges-sands,
one thereby accomplishes a vast accumulation of roots of goodness and merit.
If there is a bhikṣu who, on the eighth, thirteenth, fourteenth, or fifteenth day of the month,
bathes, maintains ritual purity, and puts on fresh, clean robes.
For one day and one night, they shall abstain from food and drink;
or at times, they may consume only the three kinds of pure food.
Circumambulating the Buddha stūpa while reciting this dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times.
Sins committed over hundreds of thousands of kalpas, as well as the five deeds of immediate retribution,
shall all be eradicated. I, Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin,
will manifest my body before them and cause all their aspirations to be completely fulfilled.
One shall behold all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas.
If one recites it two hundred and eight times, one will attain all the dhyānas.
If one recites it three hundred and eight times, [one will attain further accomplishments].
One attains the Samādhi of Purifying All Obstructions.
If one recites this four hundred and eight times,
the Four Great Heavenly Kings will constantly come to approach them, manifesting their forms to provide protection.
Furthermore, their body and mind will increase in majestic power.
If one recites this five hundred and eight times,
they will gather immeasurable, incalculable, and unfathomable great roots of goodness.
If one recites this [mantra] six hundred and eight times in full,
one will attain the fundamental accomplishment of this dhāraṇī and become a celestial being who upholds the mantra.
If one recites it seven hundred and eight times,
one will attain great majesty and be endowed with radiant light.
If one recites it eight hundred and eight times, one’s mind will become pure.
If one recites it nine hundred and eight times, the five faculties will become pure.
If one recites it one thousand and eight times,
one shall attain the fruit of Srotāpanna.
If one recites it two thousand times, one shall attain the fruit of a Sakṛdāgāmin.
If one recites it three thousand times, one shall attain the fruit of an Anāgāmin.
If one recites it four thousand times, one shall attain the fruit of an Arhat.
If one recites it five thousand times, one shall attain the fruit of a Pratyekabuddha.
If one recites it six thousand times, one shall attain the stage of Samantabhadra.
If one recites it seven thousand times, one shall attain the First Ground.
If one completes eight thousand recitations, one shall attain the fifth stage (pañcamī bhūmi).
If one completes nine thousand recitations, one shall attain the Samantamukha-dhāraṇī.
If one completes ten thousand recitations, one shall attain the Immovable Stage (acalā bhūmi).
If one recites it eleven thousand times more, one shall attain the stage of a Tathāgata and achieve the marks of a Great Man and the great lion’s roar.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who wishes [to do so] in this present life:
Those who wish to accomplish great benefits through meritorious virtues should repair ancient stupas,
recite mantras, and circumambulate them one hundred and eight times to the right;
then whatever they desire in their hearts will be fulfilled without fail.
Then Śākyamuni Buddha praised Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
You are able to thus accord with the dhāraṇī methods expounded by the Tathāgata and assist in proclaiming them."
Then the Great Yakṣa Lord Vajrapāṇi addressed the Buddha,
saying, "World-Honored One,
this Dharma of the Great King of Mantras, the Dhāraṇī..."
The Tathāgatagarbha is likewise like a Buddha-stūpa;
by means of this sublime Dharma, the World-Honored One stabilizes Jambudvīpa and causes all sentient beings to attain liberation.
It will be able to perform great Buddha-work at a later time.
The Buddha said to the Lord Vajradhara:
"If this great dhāraṇī method remains in the world, it is the same as the Tathāgata being present."
Because they are able to perform the deeds of a Buddha,
even a small amount of their activity generates a great mass of merit;
how much more so the roots of goodness obtained through extensive effort!
Even if hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, were to speak, they could not exhaustively describe it.
It cannot be illustrated by what is seen by the Buddha-eye;
it is immeasurable and inexpressible.
The Vajradhara Lord asked:
"By what causes and conditions does one achieve a great accumulation of merit with little exertion?
The Buddha said: "Listen attentively; I shall explain it for you."
If bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas,
or upāsikās wish to attain the fulfillment of a great mass of merit,
they should, according to the aforementioned method, transcribe this King of Dharma among the four great dhāraṇī-mantras ninety-nine times each.
Thereafter, in front of the Buddha stūpa,
one should construct a square altar and smear the ground with cow dung.
At the four corners of the altar, place jars filled with scented water.
Incense burners were arranged in rows for offerings.
A bowl filled with fragrant flowers, water, and non-glutinous rice was placed upon the altar,
along with the three-flavored food— sesame, mung beans, and non-glutinous rice boiled together— and the three white foods.
Place each [of these] in a flask and arrange them upon the altar.
Include various fruits numbering ninety-nine,
as well as the four kinds of food and everything else required.
Furthermore, place all manner of incense and flowers upon it.
Recite the dhāraṇī mantra within the central shaft of the spire and around the four sides of the stūpa.
Enshrine the King of Mantras within the interior of the stūpa according to the ritual method.
Visualize the Buddhas of the ten directions and recite this dhāraṇī with a sincere heart.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:

Namo nava-navati-nam tathāgata-koṭīnām | Gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka-samānām || Oṃ vibhūre vimale | Pravarale śināvale | Sara sara | Sarva-tathāgata-dhātu-garbhe | Sattya-deśite svāhā | Anaye dundubhani svāhā | Sarva-deva-nāga-āyami | Buddha-adhiṣṭhāna samaya svāhā || One should burn incense and recite this dhāraṇī mantra twenty-eight times in succession.
At that moment, the eight great bodhisattvas, the eight great yakṣa kings,
the vajra-holding yakṣa lord,
the four kings, Śakra, and Brahmā, the king of gods, [all assembled].
Nārāyaṇa and Maheśvara each held that stūpa and its *cakra* and shaft with their own hands;
there were also ninety-nine billion hundred thousand nayutas of buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
They all came to this place and consecrated that stūpa;
by placing the Buddha’s relics therein through their empowerment,
they caused the stūpa to become like a great maṇi jewel.
By this, that person shall have already constructed nine hundred and ninety billion, one hundred thousand nayutas of great jeweled stūpas;
by this, they shall obtain vast roots of goodness.
Lifespan will be extended, the body purified and free from defilement;
all illnesses will be eliminated and all calamities and obstacles utterly extinguished.
Should anyone behold this stūpa, the five heinous crimes shall be eradicated.
Hearing the sound of the stupa’s bells eliminates all evil karma;
upon casting off the body, one shall be reborn in the World of Ultimate Bliss.
Should anyone hear the name of this stupa, they shall attain the stage of non-retrogression (*avaivartika*).
Even down to birds and beasts that hear its sound shall leave the realm of animals and never again undergo such rebirth;
they shall instead attain a vast accumulation of merit and virtue.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who wishes to attain fulfillment in the six pāramitās,
they should construct a square altar,
first smearing it with cow dung and subsequently covering its surface with pure earth.
Sprinkle it with fragrant water and wipe it smooth and clean.
Place five offering bowls upon the altar and transcribe each of the four aforementioned dhāraṇī mantras ninety-nine times.
Fashion ninety-nine small stupas by hand and place one copy [of the scripture] inside each stupa.
As for the mantra of the *cakra* (spire), place it within the central shaft of the spire of each small stupa.
On the altar in the procession, one should make offerings of various incenses and flowers and circumambulate it seven times, reciting this dhāraṇī as follows:

*Namo nava-navatīnāṃ tathāgatānāṃ gaṅgānadī-bālukopama-koṭī-nayuta-śatasahasrāṇām. Oṃ prabhuḥ chiriṇi chirimuri huru śarāvari svāhā.* If one receives and maintains [this practice] according to this method...
When the six pāramitās are all fully perfected,
this is equivalent to having constructed ninety-nine billion hundred thousand nayutas of stūpas made of the seven treasures, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River.
This constitutes making offerings to ninety-nine billion hundred-thousand nayutas of Tathāgatas, Arhats,
Samyaksaṃbuddhas, all with great clouds of celestial offerings and variously adorned celestial palaces.
The various celestial deities shall present offerings with divine requisites.
Those Tathāgatas will all keep these good men and women in mind,
causing them to attain a vast accumulation of roots of goodness and merit.
If there are those who, regarding this King of Mantras,
transcribe it according to the Dharma, receive and uphold it, read and recite it,
make offerings to it with reverence, and wear it upon their bodies;
By the power of this mantra, they shall protect this person,
causing all enemies, hostile factions,
and all yakṣas, rākṣasas, and pūtanas [to be subdued].
None among them could do any evil to this person;
each harboring fear, they fled and dispersed in all directions.
If anyone were to engage in conversation with that person, [they would likewise flee].
They shall also be able to eliminate the five deeds of immediate retribution.
Should anyone hear the voice of this person,
or stand within their shadow, or touch their body, [they shall likewise be purified].
It shall cause all their past obstacles and grave offenses to be completely eliminated.
No poisons shall be able to harm them;
fire shall not burn them, and water shall not sweep them away.
Malevolent spirits and demons shall find no opportunity to cause harm;
thunder and lightning shall be unable to terrify or disturb them.
They shall be constantly sustained by the collective empowerment of all the Buddhas.
All Tathāgatas will comfort and protect them with their mindful regard;
the various devas and benevolent spirits will increase their power and strength,
such that no other incantations or sorcery can subdue them.
Therefore, one should seek this dhāraṇī method in all places;
having transcribed it, place it within a stūpa by the roadside so that sentient beings passing to and fro may encounter it.
Down to the birds, beasts, moths, flies, and ants,
all shall forever leave behind all hells and evil realms,
and be reborn in the celestial palaces.
They constantly remember their past lives until they reach the stage of non-retrogression.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin,
the Vajradhara Lord, the Four Great Kings, Śakra, the Brahmā King, and the others.
And his retinue, including the gods Nārāyaṇa and Maheśvara, said:
"O son of good family, we entrust this king of dhāraṇīs to you."
One should guard, maintain, and protect it;
bearing it upon one's shoulders as if it were contained within a precious casket,
one must ensure that it does not come to an end in future times.
One should properly uphold and carefully protect it,
bestowing it upon all sentient beings of future generations so that they may see and hear it,
thereby escaping the five immediate retributions (*pañcānantarya*).
At that time, the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin,
the Vajradhara lords, the Four Great Kings, Śakra, Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, and the eight classes of devas, nāgas, and so forth, [were present].
They all prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and spoke with one voice, saying:
"We have already received the protection of the World-Honored One,
who has bestowed upon us this dhāraṇī method and the method for constructing stūpas."
All shall guard, maintain, recite, transcribe, and make offerings to it,
for the sake of protecting all sentient beings,
so that in future times those beings may all hear and know it.
We shall not fall into the hells or other evil realms.
To repay the great kindness of the Tathāgata,
we shall all together protect [this teaching] and cause it to circulate widely.
They shall revere and honor them no differently than they would the Buddha,
so that this Dharma may not be destroyed or extinguished.
The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent!"
"You have indeed been able to steadfastly guard and uphold such a dharma of dhāraṇī.
When the great assembly had heard what the Buddha spoke, they rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
